detail.longDescription: I need my training run to be bit-for-bit reproducible across: Two different GPU architectures (A100 and T4), same machine count Different cuDNN / cuBLAS versions (e.g. 8.9 vs 9.x) Mixed precision (AMP) vs full FP32 num_workers > 0 DataLoader vs num_workers = 0 Multi-GPU DDP vs single-GPU I've already done all the "standard" determinism steps: python import os, random, numpy as np, torch os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8" random.seed(0); np.random.seed(0); torch.manual_seed(0) torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False And yet the final loss after 10 epochs differs in the ~1e-6 range between A100 and T4, and diverges completely after ~2000 steps. What I've tried / ruled out: Set all seeds, worker seeds via worker_init_fn . Set PYTHONHASHSEED=0 . Disabled tf32 ( torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False ). Set deterministic algorithms globally — PyTorch raises no error, so I assumed it's fine. Compared weight hashes at step 0 — identical. Compared after step 1 — already differs. My question: How do I guarantee bit-identical training across these hardware and library configurations?
